body:
Takeover refresh by order of the maintainer (2026-11-18). New head: `3e7e22d439d88fbebae92d60e5895a3da2043b7b`. Class: DELTA

Merged main: `621682d75bfcc09115a5e09a7dd8ad0df2562952`. Old head: `95b83ca2414a2ce40a0bf987688a49d8511133f8`. After the merge, main got one more commit (`e7f5f4315`, PROCESS_VERSION 102 only). It does not touch the files of this PR.

**Conflicts and resolutions** (merge commit `3e75b6368`)

1. `crates/app/src/posting.rs`. Main moved `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` to `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (#2282: the texts are read from disk, with an `embedded()` copy for wasm32 and for a test). The PR added one row to each table. Resolution: take main's `posting.rs`. Add the PR's rows in `posting_files.rs`, at the same place (after TinyG):
   - `BUILTINS`: `("LinuxCNC", AssetFile("linuxcnc.cps"))`, with the PR's comment.
   - `MACHINES`: `("LinuxCNC 3-axis", AssetFile("linuxcnc-3axis.mch"))`, with the PR's comment.
   - `embedded()`: the two `include_str!` rows for these files. The test `the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables` requires them.
2. `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`. Main moved `PRELUDE`, `HOOKS`, `ProgramId`, `is_true` and `is_false` to `crates/post/src/post/js_host.rs`. The PR added `rigidTappingStated: false` to the prelude's `machine` object. Resolution: take main's `js.rs`. Add the same field in `js_host.rs`.

`crates/post/src/post/machine.rs` merged with no conflict. The PR's `rigidTappingStated` and main's `coordinateRotation` are in different functions.

**Edits after the merge** (commit `3e7e22d43`)

- `crates/app/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs`: the tables now hold `AssetFile` names, so the test did not compile. The test now reads the texts with `builtin_post_text("LinuxCNC")` and `builtin_machine_text("LinuxCNC 3-axis")`. It still asserts that the two names are in the tables.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/linuxcnc/*.nc` (9 files): regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. The cause is main, not this PR: main's `185a69f1e` removed the pass at the stock top Z for every dialect. The diff only removes those pass lines (195 lines). The line counts are the same as in main's `tormach` goldens.

No snapshot PNG, `CHANGELOG.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` or `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` changes. `git diff 621682d75 --name-only` shows only the files of this PR, and `posting_files.rs` and `js_host.rs`.

**Gate** (local, debug, `-j 6`)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all 91 targets pass (764 tests), with `script_linuxcnc`, `comp`, `cycle_hop`, `ream_cycle`, `bore_cycle`, `wcs_flip` and `wcs_rotate`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`: `--lib` (372 pass, `the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables` included), `conformance` (7, `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` included), `linuxcnc_post` (9), `machine` (33), `posting` (17), `post_spindle_rule_all` (5), `control_comp` (5), `wear_comp` (5), `mach4_builtin` (2), `wcs_flip_post` (10), `wcs_rotation_control` (5). All pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not run: the full app suite (the quick gate selected all 640 app steps), the ui crate, the release heavy lanes and the snapshot lanes.

**Laws that main added for posts since the PR base.** These are findings only. This refresh did not change `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`.

- WCS: the post reads `PARAM WorkOffset` (`workOffsetIndex = true`, `workOffsetMax = 9`). It does not make a second derivation. A flipped or rotated WCS is refused by the engine because the script does not set `axisInversion` or `wcsRotation`.
- Program units: the post reads `postOptions.Units` (`programUnits = "mm inch"`). It does not read `machine.units`. This is correct.
- Cycle dwell: main changed the other LinuxCNC-family posts after this PR was written. This post does not have these changes yet:
  - #2362 (`687ee194a`): LinuxCNC requires a P word on each opening G86 block. Tormach and grblHAL now write `P0` for a zero dwell. `linuxcnc.cps` writes P on G86 only when the dwell is > 0 (`onCycle`, the line with `dwell > 0 && (g === "G82" ...`). The same check applies to G89.
  - #2348 (`5858d8928`): a G83 dwell is refused by name on Tormach and grblHAL, because LinuxCNC G83 has no P word. `linuxcnc.cps` drops a G73 / G83 dwell with no message. The same applies to G85 (REAM).
  - These are not merge conflicts. The PR owner or the reviewer must decide if they are fixed in this PR or in a follow-up issue.

**Verdict: changes requested**

Read from the diff. Not built. This is a delta review of the takeover refresh (class DELTA) and a read of the full PR against `origin/main` (`e7f5f4315`). The work is under the safety floor (posted G-code).

## Blockers

The three blockers are defects that main already fixed in the other LinuxCNC-dialect posts (`tormach.cps`, `grblhal.cps`) after this PR was written. The new post repeats them. The takeover comment lists them as open. They are wrong posted G-code, so they must be fixed in this PR.

1. **G86 with a zero dwell has no P word.** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:868` and `:910`. The block is written as `G86 X.. Y.. Z.. R.. F..` when the dwell is 0. The LinuxCNC interpreter requires a P word on each opening G86 block, and it stops the program with an error when P is missing. Main fixed this in `687ee194a` (write `P0`). Write `"P" + secs(dwell)` on each opening G86 block, as `tormach.cps` does now.
2. **G89 with a zero dwell has no P word.** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:869` and `:910`. LinuxCNC also requires P on an opening G89 block. A BACKBORE with no dwell gives a G89 with no P. Main fixed this in `8426dc0be` (a back-bore with no dwell posts G85). Do the same here.
3. **A G83 dwell is dropped with no message.** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:867` and `:910`. LinuxCNC G83 has no P word. The post writes the G83 block and the dwell is lost silently. Main refuses it by name in `5858d8928`. Refuse it by name here with the same message text.

Pin the fixes: add `linuxcnc` to `ZERO_DWELL_P0` and `SECONDS` in `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs`, to `LINUXCNC_FAMILY` in `crates/post/tests/g83_dwell_linuxcnc.rs`, and to the post list of `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`.

## Delta (the takeover refresh)

- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the `BUILTINS` row, the `MACHINES` row and the two `embedded()` rows are correct. The paths agree with the new files.
- `crates/post/src/post/js_host.rs`: `rigidTappingStated: false` is in the prelude `machine` object. `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs` sets it only for a stated `rigidTapping: true`. Correct.
- `crates/app/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs`: reads the texts with `builtin_post_text` / `builtin_machine_text` and still asserts the two table names. Correct.
- The 9 regenerated goldens (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/linuxcnc/`): the diff from the old head `95b83ca24` has deletions only (188 lines, no added line). The deleted lines are the passes at the stock top (Z0, or Z2 on `face_square_40x40_stepped`) and their link rapids. I compared the motion lines (G0-G3 with X/Y/Z and F) of all 12 LinuxCNC goldens with the `grblhal` goldens on main. The 10 milling goldens are identical. The 2 drill goldens were not regenerated, and they differ only by the expected dialect words (G43, G53 retract, G99). Feeds, depths, retracts, WCS words and tool calls did not change.

## Merge check

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 3e7e22d43` gives a clean tree (`4f3f10244`). GitHub also reports `MERGEABLE`. The `conflicts` label is still on the PR. This review does not change labels.

## Checked and correct

- Provenance comment on `linuxcnc.cps`. Sources: the public LinuxCNC references and RS-274. No vendor text found. Neutral naming.
- Modal start block `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`. `G64 P` in the program unit, or `G61`.
- WCS from `PARAM WorkOffset` only (`workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax = 9`, G59.1-G59.3 for 7-9). No second derivation.
- Program units from `postOptions.Units` (#902). The end-unit word (#2189).
- Tool change: Z lift by the selected retract, `T<n> M6`, `G43 H<n>`, Z lift again. An unstated `safe_retract` with the default G53 retract is refused by name. No assumed `G53 G0 Z0`.
- `G91 G28 Z0` / `G91 G30 Z0` then `G90` moves Z only, as the LinuxCNC reference says.
- G73/G83 refuse Q <= 0. Canned cycles with no feed, or with the spindle stopped, are refused by name.
- G33.1 only with `rigidTappingStated`, seated on R over the hole. `K` = feed / rpm. G84 for a floating holder.
- Arcs with incremental IJK under a stated G91.1. R arcs are split and checked.
- Coolant M7/M8/M9 from the machine list, refused by name when the machine has no code.
- Refused by name: control compensation, tilted moves, a trip home, a tool number that is not a positive whole number.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. New Rust files are under 400 lines. The tests are in the correct crates and each has a Gate map. `Changelog:` line is present.
- MCP: the post and the machine are rows in the tables that the existing post and machine commands read. The MCP tools reach them through those commands. No new command, so no new MCP tool is necessary.

## Non-blockers

- `PECK` (G73) and `REAM` (G85) with a dwell also drop the dwell with no message (`linuxcnc.cps:866`, `:910`). `tormach.cps` on main does the same for G73, so this is not new in this PR. Consider a refusal by name, or file a follow-up issue.
- The PR body says the rows are in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`. After the refresh they are in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. Update the body.
- `G10 L20 P<n>` in `onProbeResult` uses `#5420-#5422`, which are in the current WCS. When `SetWorkOffset` names a different WCS than the active one, the value is in the wrong system. `tormach.cps` has the same pattern.

## Not checked

- No build, no test run, no clippy. The gate results in the takeover comment were not reproduced.
- The `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/linuxcnc/*.refusal` files and `synth_linuxcnc.nc` were read only in part.
- Not run in a LinuxCNC sim or on a machine.

Needs changes before merge.

The refresh merges main cleanly and the head is mergeable. I read the remerge-diff of `3e75b6368`: main's registry split into `posting_files.rs` and `js_host.rs` took main's files, and the LinuxCNC entries were re-applied in the right places (BUILTINS after TinyG, MACHINES after TinyG 3-axis, both `embedded()` arms, `rigidTappingStated` in the prelude). The `3e7e22d43` test-fix commit follows main's file-backed registry. No logic was lost in the conflict resolution.

Local results (built and tested on this head):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites passed, including `script_linuxcnc` and the 11 recorded refusal goldens.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test linuxcnc_conformance` set: `linuxcnc_post` 9 passed; `conformance` 7; `machine` 33; `control_comp` 5; `wear_comp` 5; `post_spindle_rule_all` 5. 0 failed.
- The post refuses each unknown cycle by name, refuses an unstated safe retract, and states no PathPilot assumptions. The word-whitelist check in every golden is good practice.

Requested before merge - the canned-cycle P word in `onCycle`:

1. A DEEP cycle dwell is dropped in silence. `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:183` carries `p.dwell` on the Deep cycle, so `P > 0` reaches the post. The LinuxCNC reference (2.9, your own source) gives G83 no P word. The code lists the dwell on G82, G84, G86 and G89 only, so a deep-peck dwell posts no dwell and no message. Issue #2348 set the law: refuse it by name, not drop. `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:710-715` is the pattern to copy. Add a refusal test.
2. A BORE cycle with dwell 0 posts `G86 ... F` with no P. Issue #2362 quoted the interpreter: the first G86 block of a cycle must carry P (`NCE_DWELL_TIME_P_WORD_MISSING_WITH_G86`), so this block alarms on the control. The sibling posts fixed this in `tormach.cps:1294`: write `P` + `secs(dwell)` on G86 always, P0 included. Do the same here, and pin it with a golden.
3. A BACKBORE always posts G89, and the CL gives the BackBore cycle dwell 0 (`cycle.rs:183-184`). The G89 word list shows P, and the control reads P modally in dwell cycles (#2360: "a G89 with no P word would leave the dwell to the control's modal P"). The sibling posts map a no-dwell back-bore to G85 (#2360). Check the interpreter's first-block P rule for G89 (and for G84, whose P your code writes only when the dwell is above 0): either write the P word the reference requires, including P0, or follow #2360 and use G85 for the no-dwell back-bore. Pin each case with a golden, and say in the decision file which quote of the reference decided it.

Suggested, not blocking:

4. Add the same named refusal for a G73 and a G85 dwell, as #2356 did for the Fanuc family. The CL sends no dwell for PECK and REAM today, so only case 1 is live; the refusal keeps a future generator from dropping one in silence.
5. `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` is 406 lines now, past the 400-line rule. Split the two registries and `embedded()` along a seam, or file the split as a `P7` follow-up.
6. Body refresh: the "Base" and quick-gate lines describe the pre-refresh head (`fac6c8e8d`, `95b83ca24`, macOS), and the registration line names `posting.rs`. Update them for `3e7e22d43`.

Clean-room: the provenance header names only the public LinuxCNC 2.9 references and our own posts. Good.

The PR is a draft; I leave it as its author set it. This work is under the safety floor (posted G-code). A second, read-only review at effort:high is needed for the P-word fixes.

Review fixes for the three blockers of the review on `3e7e22d43`.

New head: `0c17caa79e10a7276ac9814cbf77c08211d7193f`. The fixes copy the behaviour of the fixes on `main` in `tormach.cps` and `grblhal.cps`.

## Blockers

1. **G86 with zero dwell.** Each opening `G86` block now writes `"P" + secs(dwell)`, `P0` for no dwell (as `687ee194a`, #2362). Pinned by `canned_posts_write_g86_and_no_other_cycle` and `a_bore_dwell_posts_as_p_in_seconds_on_the_linuxcnc_family` (`crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs`: `linuxcnc` added to `ZERO_DWELL_P0` and `SECONDS`).
2. **G89 with zero dwell.** A back-bore with no dwell now posts `G85` (as `8426dc0be`, #2360). Pinned by `dwell_to_zero_leaves_no_p_active` and the other tests of `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs` (`linuxcnc` added to `POSTS`).
3. **G83 dwell.** A positive `G83` dwell is now refused by name, with the message text of `5858d8928` (#2348). Pinned by `linuxcnc_family_refuses_a_g83_dwell_by_name` and `linuxcnc_family_posts_g83_without_dwell_unchanged` (`crates/post/tests/g83_dwell_linuxcnc.rs`: `linuxcnc` added to `LINUXCNC_FAMILY`).

I ran the three post test binaries against the old `linuxcnc.cps`. Each blocker test failed: `canned_posts_write_g86_and_no_other_cycle`, `dwell_to_zero_leaves_no_p_active`, `linuxcnc_family_refuses_a_g83_dwell_by_name`.

**Verdict: ready**

Read from the diff. Not built. No test was run. This is the Opus second review of the P-word fixes (delta `3e7e22d43..0c17caa79`, one commit). The work is under the safety floor (posted G-code). The SlaveSession re-review of this head is still necessary before a merge.

## Blockers

None.

## The three fixes (lines at `0c17caa79`, `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`)

1. **G86 P0 (#2362, model `687ee194a`).** Line 919 writes `"P" + secs(dwell)` on each opening G86 block. This is the same condition as `grblhal.cps:738` and `tormach.cps:1296` on main. Modal repeat lines (909-910) write X Y only, as on main. A dwell change reopens the group: the signature (line 908) holds the raw `p.P`, so the new opening block writes its own P (`P0` after `P0.5`). Main puts `secs(dwell)` in the signature. This post also puts `p.P` and `FeedRate` in it for all cycles. That is stricter, and it is safe: it can only write more opening blocks.
2. **Back-bore with no dwell posts G85 (#2360, model `8426dc0be`).** Line 871 is the same as `grblhal.cps` and `tormach.cps:1238` on main. A dwell that changes to 0 inside a run gives `G80`, then an opening `G85` block with no P. No modal P stays active, because G85 does not read P. The LinuxCNC G-code reference gives G85 as feed to Z, then feed out to R, and G89 as G85 with a dwell at the bottom. So G85 is the correct motion for a back-bore with no dwell. A back-bore with a dwell still posts G89 with P in seconds (line 919). That branch did not change.
3. **G83 dwell refused (#2348, model `5858d8928`).** Lines 898-902. The message text is the same as main. The refusal comes before `spindleStopped`, `xyFirst` and `cycleSeat`, so no block of that hole is written. `msg()` calls `message()`, and the host counts it as a warning. `crates/app/src/posting.rs:707` on main blocks the whole program when a warning is present ("post blocked"). So the refusal is visible, and no partial program is given as good output.

Dwell values, the same in each branch as on main:
- A negative or non-finite P gives `dwell = 0` (line 862, `has()` at line 128 checks `isFinite`). G86 then writes `P0`, a back-bore posts G85, and G83 is not refused.
- The unit is seconds (`secs`, line 825: three decimals, trailing zeros removed). This agrees with the LinuxCNC reference for P.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_cycle.rs`: `canned_posts_write_g86_and_no_other_cycle` asserts the word `P0` on each G86 line for `linuxcnc`. `a_bore_dwell_posts_as_p_in_seconds_on_the_linuxcnc_family` asserts `P0.5`. With the old script, the first test fails (no P on G86).
- `dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`: `dwell_to_zero_leaves_no_p_active` asserts the sequence `(G89, P0.5), (G85, none)` and a single `(G85, none)`. With the old script it fails (G89 with no P). `linuxcnc_family_g86_rewrites_p_when_the_dwell_changes` (`POSTS[3..]`) now includes `linuxcnc`.
- `g83_dwell_linuxcnc.rs`: asserts the refusal text with the dwell value, and asserts that no G83 line is written. The second test asserts `Q3` and no P for a dwell of 0. With the old script the first test fails.
- Each test asserts the words in the output and that the warnings are empty. The author reports that the three tests failed against the old script. I did not run them.

## Delta scope

The delta changes only `linuxcnc.cps` (lines 869-871, 898-902, 917-919) and the three test lists and Gate maps. No golden, no snapshot PNG, no other post, and no feed, depth, retract, WCS or tool word changed. `synth_linuxcnc.nc` has no G86 or G89 line, and its G83 line has no dwell, so no golden is stale. No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` outside tests. The test files are 304, 213 and 130 lines.

## Merge check

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 0c17caa79` (main at `1613e42f9`) gives a clean tree `60b8c2334`.

## Non-blockers

- `bore_cycle.rs` has `grblhal_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0` and `tormach_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0` (the transition `P0.5` then `P0`). There is no `linuxcnc_zero_dwell_g86_has_p0`. The code path is the same, but one more line pins the transition for this post.
- `linuxcnc` is not in the `GOLDEN` list of `bore_cycle.rs`. The word asserts pin the fix. A bore golden is optional.
- The G83 refusal text has "G83" and "dwell". It is the same text as main, and "(deep peck)" names the operation for the user. If the plain-English rule for messages applies, change it in all three posts in one follow-up, not here.
- Not in this delta, from the earlier reviews: a G73 or G85 dwell is dropped with no message. Main's `tormach.cps` does the same.
- The PR body quick-gate line still names the old head `95b83ca24`. The gate results for `0c17caa79` are in the author comment only.

## Not checked

- No build, no test run, no clippy. The author's gate results for this head were not reproduced.
- Line 919 also writes P on G84 with a dwell. Main's `tormach.cps` does not. This was in the earlier head, not in this delta. I did not check it against the LinuxCNC G84 reference.
- Not run in a LinuxCNC simulator or on a machine.

**Verdict: ready**

Built and tested locally at this head. This is the SlaveSession re-review of the fix head `0c17caa79`. It closes the three blockers of my review at `3e7e22d43`. It adds the build evidence that the read-only Opus review at this head asked for. I did not write this change.

## Blockers

None.

## The three blockers, fixed and pinned

1. **G86 writes P on each opening block (#2362).** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:919` writes `"P" + secs(dwell)` for G86, so a zero dwell posts `P0`. This matches `tormach.cps:1296` and `grblhal.cps:738`. Pinned by `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs`.
2. **A back-bore with no dwell posts G85 (#2360).** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:871` selects `G89` only when the dwell is greater than 0, otherwise `G85`. No modal P stays active, because G85 does not read P. Pinned by `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs` (`dwell_to_zero_leaves_no_p_active`).
3. **A G83 dwell is refused by name (#2348).** `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:898-902`. The refusal comes before the block is written, so the post writes no G83 line. The message text is the same as main's. Pinned by `crates/post/tests/g83_dwell_linuxcnc.rs`.

## Local results

Run in a worktree at `0c17caa79`, debug profile, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test bore_cycle --test dwell_cycles_modal_p --test g83_dwell_linuxcnc` — 9 + 5 + 2 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test bore_cycle --test linuxcnc_post` — 4 + 9 pass.
- Full `camcraft-post` suite — 0 failed in every test binary.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post` — clean.
- The `linuxcnc` goldens have no G85, G86 or G89 line, and no golden changed. This agrees with the "No golden changes" line of the author comment.

## Merge check

GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`. The Opus review ran `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 0c17caa79` and got a clean tree.

## Non-blockers

- The PR body quick-gate line names the old head `95b83ca24`. Put the gate results for `0c17caa79` in the body.
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` is 406 lines. It is 6 lines over the 400-line rule. PR #2554 moves `post_offer` to its own file and brings it back under 400. Do nothing here.
- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` has the `P0.5` then `P0` transition tests for `grblhal` and `tormach`, not for `linuxcnc`. One more line would pin the transition for this post. Optional.
- G73 and G85 with a dwell still drop the dwell with no message. Main's `tormach.cps` does the same. If we want a refusal, file a follow-up issue.

## Not checked

- Not run in a LinuxCNC simulator or on a machine.
- No full-workspace build. I built and tested `camcraft-post` and the two `camcraft-app` suites that the diff touches.
